scenario.name: PostgreSQL Security & SigmaHQ DFIR — PostgreSQL COPY FROM PROGRAM & Large Object (pg_largeobject) Execution Forensics
scenario.overview: An archive database manager normally imports and exports neat index tables, yet one special shipping privilege lets it feed a table straight from an external workshop tool. Investigators track a privileged sign-in using that import feature to run live floor commands and export a custom binary library right onto the archive disk. In this scenario (T1078, PostgreSQL Security & SigmaHQ DFIR, PostgreSQL COPY FROM PROGRAM & Large Object , pg_largeobject Execution Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: privileged Role Authentication, then cOPY FROM PROGRAM OS Command Execution, then large Object Shared Library Drop. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Privileged Role Authentication, then COPY FROM PROGRAM OS Command Execution, then Large Object Shared Library Drop, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 5432 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Privileged Role Authentication & pg_execute_server_program Check in postgresql.log
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1078 - Valid Accounts: PostgreSQL Superuser Role)

stages.title: Stage 2: COPY ... FROM PROGRAM OS Command Execution & Linux auditd /bin/sh Child Trace
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.004 - Unix Shell Spawned by postgres Backend)
stages.description: Next, the caller submits a table-import slip instructing the archive clerk to launch a command-line helper and pour its printed output straight into a temporary holding table, an action immediately filmed by the building security camera. The actor executes COPY cmd_exec FROM PROGRAM 'id; uname -a' (introduced in PostgreSQL 9.3, tracked under CVE-2019-9193 as a feature design risk). FROM PROGRAM , CVE-2019-9193 Context so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
